intro: List Python ka sabse zyada use hone wala mutable container hai, aur uske methods hi usse useful banate hain. append se ek item jodo, extend se poori list, sort se order badlo — har method ka ek return value aur ek mutation rule hota hai. Ye section wahi methods practice karata hai jo daily code me aate hain.
theory: Mutating methods list ko in-place badalte hain aur zyadatar None return karte hain. Isliye `items = items.append(x)` likhna items ko None bana deta hai — return value par nahi, side effect par bharosa karo.
append ek item jodta hai, extend ek iterable ke saare items jodta hai, aur insert position par ek item daalta hai. Teenon list ki length badalte hain, par alag tarike se.
remove value se delete karta hai aur missing value par ValueError deta hai; pop index se delete karta hai aur hataya hua item return karta hai. `del items[i]` return nahi karta.
sort in-place hai aur original list badal deta hai; sorted() nayi list deta hai. `key=` se comparison rule badalta hai, `reverse=True` se order ulta hota hai.
copy() shallow copy deta hai: naya list object banta hai par andar ke mutable items share hote hain. Nested data ke liye copy.deepcopy chahiye.
syntax:
items = ['pen', 'book']
items.append('bag')        # ek item
items.extend(['cap', 'box'])  # poora iterable
items.insert(0, 'first')   # position par

items.sort()              # in-place, return None
items.sort(reverse=True)  # descending
items = sorted(items, key=len)  # naya list
last = items.pop()        # delete + return
items.remove('book')      # value se delete

items.index(value)       # pehla position, warna ValueError
items.count(value)       # kitni baar aaya
items.reverse()          # in-place ulta
copy_of = items.copy()   # shallow copy

explain: index pehla position deta hai, count occurrences ginta hai.
Output ko print se verify karo.
Ye List Methods ka basic building block hai.
sort in-place order badalta hai aur None return karta hai.
Ek step aur jodne se behaviour kaise badalta hai, dekho.
Input badal kar edge case test karo.

examples.code:
rows = [
    {'name': 'Asha', 'score': 91},
    {'name': 'Ravi', 'score': 78},
    {'name': 'Meera', 'score': 85},
]
rows.sort(key=lambda row: row['score'], reverse=True)
print([row['name'] for row in rows[:2]])
print([row['name'] for row in rows])
explain: sort key function se dict rows ko score par order karta hai, bina data copy kiye.
Ye snippet end-to-end flow dikhata hai.
Output ko project/interview me evidence ki tarah use karo.

realWorld: ETL jobs me rows ki list par append/extend hota hai; galti se `rows = rows.append(row)` likhne se poora batch None ban jata hai aur next step crash karta hai.
Top-N reports me `sort(key=..., reverse=True)[:10]` ka pattern aata hai. In-place sort tab khatarnak hai jab wahi list caller ke paas bhi ho.
Shopping cart ya queue jaisi lists me pop(0) O(n) hota hai; bade queues ke liye collections.deque use karna chahiye.

interview.q: append aur extend me kya fark hai?
interview.a: append ek object jodta hai — agar list pass ki to wahi list ek element ban jati hai. extend iterable ko khol kar uske items jodta hai. Length aur nesting dono alag ho jate hain.

interview.q: sort() aur sorted() me kab kya use karoge?
interview.a: Jab original list badalni ho aur return value ki zaroorat na ho to list.sort(). Jab original bachani ho ya kisi bhi iterable (tuple, generator) ko sort karna ho to sorted(), jo nayi list deta hai.

interview.q: list.copy() shallow kyun hai?
interview.a: Ye sirf naya outer list banata hai; andar ke objects wahi references hain. Nested list/dict badalne par dono copies me change dikhta hai. Deep copy ke liye copy.deepcopy use karo.

interview.q: pop(0) kyun slow hai aur alternative kya hai?
interview.a: List array-backed hai, isliye index 0 hatane par baaki sab elements shift hote hain — O(n). Queue ke liye collections.deque ka popleft() O(1) hai.

debugging.error: TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str
debugging.why: String concatenation ko dono taraf str chahiye; Python implicit conversion nahi karta. Ye List Methods ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: f-string ya str() se explicit conversion karo.
debugging.lesson: TypeError type mismatch batata hai — conversion explicit karo.

debugging.error: IndexError: list index out of range
debugging.why: List me sirf 0 aur 1 index hain; 5 par kuch nahi. Ye List Methods ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: Index se pehle length check karo ya safe getter use karo.
debugging.correct:
scores = [10, 20]
print(scores[1] if len(scores) > 1 else None)
debugging.lesson: IndexError off-by-one aur empty collection ka signal hai.

debugging.why: Dict me score key exist nahi karti; [] missing key par KeyError deta hai. Ye List Methods ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: get() se default do ya key ki presence check karo.
debugging.lesson: KeyError expected-missing field ka case hai — get/default se handle karo.

debugging.error: ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '12.5'
debugging.why: int() sirf poore number ka string parse karta hai. Ye List Methods ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: Pehle float() phir int() karo, ya Decimal use karo.
debugging.lesson: ValueError format ka issue hai, type ka nahi.

revision: List Methods: revise append — append ek item ko list ke end me jodta hai aur None return karta hai.
List Methods: revise extend — extend doosri iterable ke saare items ek-ek karke jodta hai.
List Methods: revise insert — insert position par item daalta hai aur baaki items ko aage shift karta hai.
List Methods: revise remove — remove pehli matching value hatata hai; value na mile to ValueError aata hai.
List Methods: revise pop — pop index se item hatata hai aur hataya hua item return karta hai.
